courses.title: 可可英语名著精读
courses.description: 可可英语精选经典名著双语对照课文，含英文原文与中文翻译

lessons.title: 悉达多-婆罗门之子(1)
transcript: In the shade of the house, in the sunshine of the riverbank near the boats, in the shade of the Sal-wood forest, in the shade of the fig tree is where Siddhartha grew up, the handsome son of the Brahman, the young falcon, together with his friend Govinda, son of a Brahman.
The sun tanned his light shoulders by the banks of the river when bathing, performing the sacred ablutions, the sacred offerings.

In the mango grove, shade poured into his black eyes, when playing as a boy, when his mother sang, when the sacred offerings were made, when his father, the scholar, taught him, when the wise men talked.
For a long time, Siddhartha had been partaking in the discussions of the wise men, practising debate with Govinda, practising with Govinda the art of reflection, the service of meditation.

He already knew how to speak the Om silently, the word of words, to speak it silently into himself while inhaling, to speak it silently out of himself while exhaling, with all the concentration of his soul, the forehead surrounded by the glow of the clear-thinking spirit.
He already knew to feel Atman in the depths of his being, indestructible, one with the universe.
Joy leapt in his father's heart for his son who was quick to learn, thirsty for knowledge; he saw him growing up to become great wise man and priest, a prince among the Brahmans.

Bliss leapt in his mother's breast when she saw him, when she saw him walking, when she saw him sit down and get up, Siddhartha, strong, handsome, he who was walking on slender legs, greeting her with perfect respect.
Love touched the hearts of the Brahmans' young daughters when Siddhartha walked through the lanes of the town with the luminous forehead, with the eye of a king, with his slim hips.
He was the wonder of the town, the pride of the family.
translation: 在房舍的阴影中，在阳光照耀下的河岸边，在泊岸的小船旁，在柳树林和无花果树的浓荫里，悉达多，英俊的婆罗门之子，年少的雄鹰，与挚友侨文达一同长大。
在河岸边，在神圣的祭祀和沐浴中，阳光晒黑了他浅色的臂膀。
在芒果林中。在孩童的嬉戏间，在母亲的歌声和神圣的祭祀中，在聆听博学父亲的教诲和智者的谈话时，树影流入了他幽黑的眼眸。
悉达多早已加入了智者们的谈话，与侨文达一道修习辩论、静思与禅定的技艺。
他已经学会如何默念"唵"--这真言之本；吸气时默默吸入它，呼气时则凝神默默吐出它，此刻，他的前额仿佛放射出纯净思索的心灵之光。
他已学会如何在自我存在的深层体认识阿特曼--永恒不坏，与宇宙合一。
他的父亲心中充满喜悦，因为他的儿子聪慧好学且渴慕知识；他知道他的儿子将会成为一位伟大的智者、一位祭祀、婆罗门中的王子。
他的母亲满怀幸福地看着自己的儿子，注视着他坐落、起立和行走，强壮英俊的悉达多，四肢修长，体态完美地向母亲问安。
每当悉达多走过城里的街巷，年轻的婆罗门女子心中就会泛起阵阵爱的涟漪；他有着高高的前额，王者般的眼神，还有隙削的背景。
这位少年在城中极受大家欢迎，是整个家族的骄傲。

lessons.title: 《爱丽丝漫游奇境》- 1
transcript: Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the bank, and of having nothing to do.

So she was considering in her own mind whether the pleasure of making a daisy-chain would be worth the trouble of getting up and picking the daisies, when suddenly a White Rabbit with pink eyes ran close by her.
There was nothing so very remarkable in that; but when the Rabbit actually took a watch out of its waistcoat-pocket, and looked at it, and then hurried on, Alice started to her feet.
In another moment down went Alice after it, never once considering how in the world she was to get out again.

The rabbit-hole went straight on like a tunnel for some way, and then dipped suddenly down, so suddenly that Alice had not a moment to think about stopping herself before she found herself falling down a very deep well.
Either the well was very deep, or she fell very slowly, for she had plenty of time as she went down to look about her and to wonder what was going to happen next.
She took down a jar from one of the shelves as she passed; it was labelled 'ORANGE MARMALADE', but to her great disappointment it was empty.
'I wonder how many miles I've fallen by this time?' she said aloud. 'I must be getting somewhere near the centre of the earth.'
'Dinah'll miss me very much to-night, I should think!' (Dinah was the cat.) 'I hope they'll remember her saucer of milk at tea-time.'
Down, down, down. Would the fall never come to an end? ... thump! thump! down she came upon a heap of sticks and dry leaves, and the fall was over.

Alice was not a bit hurt, and she jumped up on to her feet in a moment; she looked up, but it was all dark overhead; before her was another long passage, and the White Rabbit was still in sight, hurrying down it.

There were doors all round the hall, but they were all locked; and when Alice had been all the way down one side and up the other, trying every door, she walked sadly down the middle, wondering how she was ever to get out again.
Alice opened the door and found that it led into a small passage, not much larger than a rat-hole: she knelt down and looked along the passage into the loveliest garden you ever saw.
However, this bottle was not marked 'poison,' so Alice ventured to taste it, and finding it very nice, she very soon finished it off.
'What a curious feeling!' said Alice; 'I must be shutting up like a telescope.'
And so it was indeed: she was now only ten inches high, and her face brightened up at the thought that she was now the right size for going through the little door into that lovely garden.
She ate a little bit, and said anxiously to herself, 'Which way? Which way?' ... she was quite surprised to find that she remained the same size.
So she set to work, and very soon finished off the cake.
translation: 爱丽丝开始对坐在姐姐身边的无聊生活感到厌倦，无所事事地打发时间。
她正想着采雏菊编花环是否值得那么麻烦，突然一只粉眼睛的白兔从身边跑过。
没什么特别的，但当兔子真的从背心口袋里掏出怀表看了一眼又匆忙离开时，爱丽丝猛地站了起来。
爱丽丝立刻追了上去，压根没想过自己该怎么回来。
兔子洞像隧道一样向前延伸，然后突然向下倾斜，爱丽丝来不及想如何停下，就发现自己正掉进一口深井。
要么井非常深，要么她掉得很慢，因为她有充足的时间环顾四周，好奇接下来会发生什么。
她经过时从架子上取下一个罐子，上面写着“橘子酱”，但令她失望的是，罐子是空的。
“不知道我掉了多少英里了？”她大声说，“我快到地心了吧。”
“今晚丁丁会想念我的。”（丁丁是那只猫）“希望他们别忘了给丁丁留晚饭的牛奶。”
掉啊，掉啊，掉啊。这无尽的坠落何时是个头？……扑通！扑通！她终于掉在了一堆枯枝干叶上，坠落结束了。
爱丽丝毫发无伤，立刻跳了起来；她抬头望去，头顶一片漆黑；面前是一条长长的通道，白兔还在前面急匆匆地跑着。
大厅四周都是门，但全都锁着。爱丽丝把一侧的门全试了一遍又从另一侧返回，沮丧地走在中间，不知该如何出去。
爱丽丝打开门，发现那是一条只比老鼠洞大一点的通道；她跪下望去，尽头是一个她从未见过的美丽花园。
好在这瓶上并没有标“毒药”，爱丽丝大着胆子尝了一口，味道不错，她很快就喝光了。
“这感觉真奇妙！”爱丽丝说，“我像望远镜一样正在缩起来。”
确实如此：她现在只有十英寸高，一想到自己正好能穿过小门进花园，她脸上的光彩就亮了起来。
她吃了一点， anxiously 对自己说：“往哪边？往哪边？”……她惊讶地发现自己身高没变。
于是她继续吃，很快就吃完了整块蛋糕。

lessons.title: 《爱丽丝漫游奇境》- 2
transcript: Poor Alice! It was as much as she could do, lying down on one side, to look through into the garden with one eye; but to get through was more hopeless than ever: she sat down and began to cry again.
She went on all the same, shedding gallons of tears, until there was a large pool all round her, about four inches deep and reaching half down the hall.
It was the White Rabbit returning, splendidly dressed, with a pair of white kid gloves in one hand and a large fan in the other.
Alice took up the fan and gloves, and, as the hall was very hot, she kept fanning herself all the time she went on talking.
I wonder if I've been changed in the night? Let me think: was I the same when I got up this morning?
However, she soon made out that she was in the pool of tears which she had wept when she was nine feet high.
Everything is so out-of-the-way down here, that I should think very likely it can talk: at any rate, there's no harm in trying.
They were indeed a queer-looking party that assembled on the bank—the birds with draggled feathers, the animals with their fur clinging close to them, and all dripping wet, cross, and uncomfortable.
The first question of course was, how to get dry again: they had a consultation about this, and after a few minutes it seemed quite natural to Alice to find herself talking familiarly with them.
Why," said the Dodo, "the best way to explain it is to do it."
Everybody has won, and all must have prizes.
Mine is a long and a sad tale!" said the Mouse, turning to Alice, and sighing.
It was the White Rabbit, trotting slowly back again, and looking anxiously about as it went, as if it had lost something.
Why, Mary Ann, what are you doing out here? Run home this moment, and fetch me a pair of gloves and a fan! Quick, now!
I know something interesting is sure to happen," she said to herself, "whenever I eat or drink anything; so I'll just see what this bottle does.
translation: 可怜的爱丽丝！她侧着身子，费了多大劲才用一只眼睛望进花园；可是要穿过去比以往任何时候都更没希望了：她坐下来，又哭了起来。
她还是不停地哭，流了成加仑的眼泪，直到四周形成一个大水池，大约四英寸深，淹没了半个大厅。
回来的是白兔，衣冠楚楚，一只手拿着一副白色小山羊皮手套，另一只手拿着一把大扇子。
爱丽丝拿起扇子和手套，因为大厅里很热，她一边说话一边不停地扇着扇子。
我想知道我夜里是不是变了？让我想想：我今天早上起床的时候，还是原来那个我吗？
然而，她很快就发现，自己正处在九英尺高时哭出来的那片眼泪池里。
这里的一切都那么稀奇古怪，我觉得它很可能会说话：不管怎样，试试总没有坏处。
聚集在岸边的确实是一群稀奇古怪的家伙——羽毛湿漉漉的鸟儿，毛紧贴在身上的动物，全都湿淋淋的，又生气又不舒服。
第一个问题自然是如何把身子弄干：他们为此商量了几分钟，爱丽丝发现自己和他们谈笑风生，仿佛相识了一辈子，这使她觉得很自然。
渡渡鸟说："解释这件事的最好办法就是亲自做一遍。"
"每个人都赢了，而且大家都必须得奖。"
"我的故事很长，而且很悲伤！"老鼠说着转向爱丽丝，叹了口气。
走回来的是白兔，它一边慢吞吞地小跑着，一边不安地四下张望，好像丢了什么东西似的。
"喂，玛丽·安，你在这里干什么？立刻跑回家去，给我拿一副手套和一把扇子来！快，现在！"
"我知道只要吃点或喝点什么，就一定会发生有趣的事，"她对自己说，"所以我倒要看看这瓶东西能把我怎么样。"

lessons.title: 《简·爱》- 1
transcript: What is all this? demanded another voice peremptorily; and Mrs. Reed came along the corridor, her cap flying wide, her gown rustling stormily.
Abbott and Bessie, I believe I gave orders that Jane Eyre should be left in the red-room till I came to her myself.
Miss Jane screamed so loud, ma'am, pleaded Bessie.
Let her go, was the only answer.
Come here, Miss Jane: your name is Jane, is it not?
Yes, sir, Jane Eyre.
Well, you have been crying, Miss Jane Eyre; can you tell me what about? Have you any pain?
No, sir.
Oh! I daresay she is crying because she could not go with Missis in the carriage, interposed Bessie.
Surely not! why, she is too old for such pettishness.
translation: “这是怎么回事？”一个专横的声音问道；里德太太沿着走廊走来，帽子歪戴着，衣服沙沙作响。
“阿博特和贝西，我相信我命令过，把简·爱关在红房子里，直到我亲自来。”
“小姐简叫得可响了，夫人。”贝西说。
“放开她。”这就是唯一的回答。
“到这儿来，简小姐：你的名字是简，不是吗？”
“是的，先生，简·爱。”
“怎么了，简·爱小姐，你在哭什么？你哪儿疼吗？”
“不，先生。”
“哦！我敢说她哭是因为她没能跟太太一起坐马车。”贝西插嘴说。
“胡说！她都这么大了，怎么可能耍小性子。”

lessons.title: 《傲慢与偏见》- 1
transcript: Mr. Darcy corroborated it with a bow, and was beginning to determine not to fix his eyes on Elizabeth, when they were suddenly arrested by the sight of the stranger, and Elizabeth happening to see the countenance of both as they looked at each other, was all astonishment at the effect of the meeting.
Both changed colour, one looked white, the other red. Mr. Wickham, after a few moments, touched his hat -- a salutation which Mr. Darcy just deigned to return.
What could be the meaning of it? -- It was impossible to imagine; it was impossible not to long to know.
In another minute Mr. Bingley, but without seeming to have noticed what passed, took leave and rode on with his friend.
Mr. Collins was not a sensible man, and the deficiency of nature had been but little assisted by education or society.

The greatest part of his life having been spent under the guidance of an illiterate and miserly father; and though he belonged to one of the universities, he had merely kept the necessary terms, without forming at it any useful acquaintance.

The subjection in which his father had brought him up had given him originally great humility of manner, but it was now a good deal counteracted by the self-conceit of a weak head, living in retirement, and the consequential feelings of early and unexpected prosperity.

A fortunate chance had recommended him to Lady Catherine de Bourgh when the living of Hunsford was vacant; and the respect which he felt for her high rank and his veneration for her as his patroness, mingling with a very good opinion of himself, of his authority as a clergyman, and his rights as a rector, made him altogether a mixture of pride and obsequiousness, self-importance and humility.
translation: 达西证明他没有撒谎，同时鞠了个躬。达西正打算把眼睛从伊丽莎白身上移开，这时突然看到了那个陌生人。只见他们两人面面相觑，大惊失色，伊丽莎白看到这个邂逅相遇的场合，觉得很是惊奇。
两个人都变了脸色，一个惨白，一个通红，过了一会儿，韦翰先生按了按帽子，达西先生勉强回了一下礼。这是什么意思呢？既叫人无从想象，又叫人不能不想去打听一下。
又过了一会儿，彬格莱先生若无其事地跟她们告别了，骑着马跟他朋友管自走了。
柯林斯先生并不是个通情达理的人，他虽然也受过教育，也踏进了社会，但是先天的缺陷却简直没有得到什么弥补。
他大部分日子是在他那守财奴的文盲父亲的教导下度过的。他也算进过大学，实际上不过照例住了几个学期，并没有结交一个有用的朋友。
他的父亲管束得他十分严厉，因此他的为人本来很是谦卑，不过他本是个蠢材，现在生活又过得很优闲，当然不免自高自大，何况年纪轻轻就发了意外之财，更其自视甚高，哪里还谈得上谦卑。
当时汉斯福教区有个牧师空缺，他鸿运享通，得到了咖苔琳·德·包尔夫人的提拔。他看到他的女施主地位颇高，便悉心崇拜，备加尊敬；另方面又自命不凡，自以为当上了教士，该有怎样怎样的权利，于是他一身兼有了骄傲自大和谦卑顺从的两重性格。

lessons.title: 《小王子》- 1
transcript: Once when I was six years old I saw a magnificent picture in a book, called Stories from Nature, about the primeval forest.
It was a picture of a boa constrictor, in the process of swallowing a wild animal.
He kept the whole forest under his control, and no one dared to disobey him.
I thought to myself: if I could draw, I would draw a picture of a boa constrictor digesting an elephant.
But I had never drawn anything in my life before.
So I drew my first picture, Number One.
It looked like this: a hat.
I showed my drawing to the grown-ups, and asked them whether it was beautiful.
They answered me: why should a hat be beautiful? It is only a hat.
They did not understand that it was not a hat at all.
It was a boa constrictor digesting an elephant.
translation: 我六岁的时候，在一本名为《自然故事》的书里，看到了一幅关于原始森林的壮丽画面。
那是一条巨蟒正在吞食一只野兽的画面。
他把整个森林都控制在手中，没有人敢违背他的命令。
我心想：如果我会画画，我会画一幅巨蟒消化大象的画。
但我以前从没画过任何东西。
所以我画了我的第一幅画，图一号。
它看起来像这样：一顶帽子。
我把画拿给大人看，问他们这幅画美不美。
他们回答我：一顶帽子有什么好看的？不过是一顶帽子而已。
他们根本没看出来，这根本不是帽子。
这是一条正在消化大象的巨蟒。
